count_rules.note-<type>: one per pitched, non-grace, non-cue <note> element with that <type> (chord members count individually, tie continuations count)
count_rules.dot / double-dot: one per pitched, non-grace notehead (<note> element, chord members individually) with exactly one / two <dot/>; dotted rests are counted only as rest-dotted
count_rules.chord: one per chord (a <note> followed by <chord/> members)
count_rules.beam: one per beam group (level-1 <beam>begin</beam> on a non-chord-member note)
count_rules.flag: one per stem (non-grace, non-chord-member note of type eighth or shorter) without any <beam>
count_rules.ledger-above / ledger-below: one per notehead that needs ledger lines above / below its staff (position computed from pitch and the clef in force)
count_rules.grace / grace-slash: one per grace <note> element / with slash="yes"
count_rules.rest-whole-bar: one per <rest measure="yes"> not inside a multi-bar rest block
count_rules.clef-<kind>: one per <clef> element (initial clefs included; a piano grand staff has two)
count_rules.clef-change: one per <clef> element after the first measure's initial attributes
count_rules.acc-<kind>: one per <accidental> element; acc-courtesy = cautionary/parenthesized accidentals

count_rules.tie: one per <tied type="start"> (per notehead: a 3-note chord tie counts 3)
count_rules.tie-across-system: ties whose stop lies after a system break (print new-system OR new-page) relative to the start; x-tie-across-page = the subset across a page break
count_rules.tempo-mark: one per bold <words> direction at a measure start (engraved with \tempo)
count_rules.multi-page: 1 when the truth has at least one page break
count_rules.lyrics-hyphen: one per syllable with syllabic begin/middle (a hyphen follows)
count_rules.lyrics-melisma: one per syllable sung on more than one attack (a later non-tied note of the same voice before the next syllable of that verse)

counting_rules.tempo-mark: one per bold <words> direction at a measure start (engraved with \tempo)
counting_rules.multi-page: 1 when the truth has at least one page break
counting_rules.lyrics-hyphen: one per syllable with syllabic begin/middle (a hyphen follows)
counting_rules.lyrics-melisma: one per syllable sung on more than one attack (a later non-tied note of the same voice before the next syllable of that verse)
counting_rules.lyrics-multi-verse: number of lyric lines (verses) when more than one
counting_rules.stem-up / stem-down: one per stem (non-chord-member, non-grace note shorter than a whole), counted ONLY when the truth gives <stem> for every such note (two voices on one staff); otherwise absent because stem direction is left to the engraver

notes: <tuplet bracket="yes|no"> is what LilyPond printed (verified per tuplet by a TupletBracket stencil callback): the bracket is omitted when one beam spans exactly the tuplet's first to last note. LilyPond prints the actual number only ("3", "5", "2"), MusicXML default show-number="actual".

Ties are per notehead (<tie>/<tied> on each tied chord member). A tie across a system or page break is engraved as two half-ties (one at the end of the first system, one at the start of the next); the truth has ONE tie (start on the last note of the system, stop on the first note of the next).

Courtesy time signatures that LilyPond prints at the end of a system before a meter change are NOT separate <time> elements in the truth (MusicXML has no courtesy-time element; the change is the <time> in the first measure of the next system). Do not count them as extra time changes.
<beam> elements reproduce the engraved beam groups exactly (manual beaming, \autoBeamOff); a rest inside a beam carries no <beam>.

Counts follow meta.counting_rules: time-4-4 / time-2-2 count numeric signatures only, C and cut count as time-common / time-cut; a piano grand staff prints each time signature on both staves but the truth (and the count) has one <time> per measure.
Both voices are present in every measure, so the truth gives <stem> up/down for every stemmed note and stem-up/stem-down are counted.

items.title: Quartet in Changing Meters (string quartet)

expected.notes: Four single-staff parts (bracketed string quartet; viola in alto clef), 8 measures, 3 systems. All four parts change meter together in every bar: numeric 4/4, 3/4, 5/8, 7/8, 2/4, 6/8, C, cut - each part carries its own <time> (8 x 4 = 32 in the truth). Different tuplets sound at the same time: m1 eighth triplet (Vn I) against quarter triplet (Vn II); m2 quarter triplet (Vn I); m5 5:4 sixteenths (Vn I) against an eighth triplet (Vn II) and another (Va); m6 2:3 duplet (Vn II) against dotted quarters; m7 eighth triplet (Vn I). Ties: Vn I a' m1->m2, a' m3->m4 (across the system break and 5/8 -> 7/8), f'' m5->m6, e'' m6->m7 (across the system break and 6/8 -> C); Va d' m2->m3. Key A minor.
